topIssues.title: kona: BlobData::fill returns Critical on blob under-fill instead of Reset, causing permanent pipeline halt
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
## Summary

In kona's derivation pipeline, when the blob provider returns fewer blobs than there are blob-hash placeholders ("under-fill"), `BlobData::fill` returns `BlobDecodingError::InvalidLength`. This error maps through `BlobProviderError::BlobDecoding(_)` to `PipelineErrorKind::Critical` — a non-recoverable error that permanently terminates the pipeline and requires operator intervention to restart.

The Go implementation (`op-node`) wraps the equivalent condition as `NewResetError`, which is auto-recoverable: the pipeline automatically retries at the last safe L1 block.

## Under-fill is Common in Practice

This is not merely a theoretical concern. L1 providers commonly return fewer blobs than requested in two real-world scenarios:

1. **Blobs not yet available**: The provider may not have all blobs cached/synced when the pipeline first tries to fetch them for a newly confirmed L1 block.
2. **L1 block reorged out**: If the L1 block containing the blob transactions has been reorged away, the provider may return fewer (or zero) blobs. The pipeline should reset to discover the new canonical chain, not halt permanently.

In both cases the correct behavior is to reset and retry — exactly what Go does.

## Current Behavior

**kona (Rust):**
- [`blob_data.rs:155-157`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/9eaad92f7f2f8a5f9687b6a703d4afc3dad1d347/rust/kona/crates/protocol/derive/src/sources/blob_data.rs#L155): `if index >= blobs.len() { return Err(BlobDecodingError::InvalidLength); }`
- [`sources.rs:54-56`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/9eaad92f7f2f8a5f9687b6a703d4afc3dad1d347/rust/kona/crates/protocol/derive/src/errors/sources.rs#L54): `BlobProviderError::BlobDecoding(_) => PipelineError::Provider(val.to_string()).crit()`
- Result: **Critical** — pipeline terminates permanently, operator must restart

**op-node (Go):**
- [`blob_data_source.go:108-111`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/9eaad92f7f2f8a5f9687b6a703d4afc3dad1d347/op-node/rollup/derive/blob_data_source.go#L108): under-fill is returned as `NewResetError`
- [`blob_data_source.go:153-155`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/9eaad92f7f2f8a5f9687b6a703d4afc3dad1d347/op-node/rollup/derive/blob_data_source.go#L153): wrapping as reset error
- Result: **Reset** — pipeline rewinds to last safe point and retries automatically

## Proposed Fix

Change the under-fill path in `BlobData::fill` to return a Reset-level error rather than a `BlobDecodingError` (which always maps to Critical). The cleanest approach is either:

1. Return a new `BlobProviderError` variant (e.g. `BlobsUnavailable`) that maps to `Reset` in the `From<BlobProviderError> for PipelineErrorKind` impl — consistent with how `BlobNotFound` already maps to Reset, or
2. Change `BlobData::fill` to return a `PipelineErrorKind` directly for the under-fill case (bypassing `BlobDecodingError`).

Note that `BlobNotFound` already sets the correct precedent: a 404 from the beacon node maps to `ResetError::BlobsUnavailable(slot).reset()`. Under-fill should be treated similarly.

## Impact

- **Severity:** Liveness — kona derivation pipeline halts permanently on blob under-fill; op-node recovers automatically
- **Affected component:** `kona/crates/protocol/derive` — `BlobData::fill` and error mapping in `sources.rs`

## References

Found during conformance review `kona-node-vs-op-node` (issue LR-13).

topPRs.title: refactor(op-devstack): simplify acceptance testing around direct preset constructors
topPRs.author: teddyknox
topPRs.body:
## Summary

This PR completes the acceptance-test spike to simplify `op-devstack` around direct preset constructors and per-test isolated environments.

The main architectural change is that acceptance tests now construct their own system-under-test directly from preset constructors. The old orchestrator/system/registry model has been removed in favor of explicit constructor DAGs, typed runtime families, and direct references.

This also removes the remaining legacy “network target polymorphism” infrastructure, including external/live-network acceptance paths.

Net effect:
- each acceptance test gets its own fresh target
- presets are constructor-driven instead of orchestrator-driven
- tests interact with the concrete preset shape they asked for
- a large amount of legacy compatibility and ID-based plumbing is deleted

This branch is a large net deletion:
- `383 files changed`
- `9,536 insertions`
- `17,724 deletions`

## Motivation

`op-devstack` had accumulated several layers that made acceptance testing harder to reason about:

- shared package-level test environments
- generic network-target abstractions
- orchestrator/system/control-plane plumbing
- ID/registry/matcher-based lookup
- shim/sysext compatibility layers
- preset implementations that were effectively wrappers over legacy internals

That model made simple test setup complicated, encouraged cross-test coupling, and obscured how systems were actually constructed.

This PR replaces that with a simpler model:

- tests call preset constructors directly
- constructors compose lower-level constructors in a clear hierarchy
- presets return concrete system shapes
- runtime assembly uses direct references instead of IDs and registry lookups

## What Changed

### 1. Acceptance tests now use per-test isolated preset constructors

Acceptance suites were migrated away from shared `init_test.go` package setup and onto direct preset construction in the tests or test-local helpers.

This migration covers the major acceptance families, including:
- base
- batcher
- sync
- sync tester
- conductor
- interop
- proofs
- supernode
- fusaka / jovian / isthmus
- Rust `kona` supervisor/node tests
- mixed `op`/`kona` and `op-reth` proof presets

This makes test setup explicit and ensures each test runs against its own fresh network target.

### 2. External/live-network support was removed

The external network target / external EL acceptance paths were deleted.

Removed examples include:
- `op-devstack/presets/minimal_external_el.go`
- `op-devstack/sysgo/system_synctester_ext.go`
- external sync-tester acceptance suites

This narrows the framework to the local constructor-driven model and removes a large amount of branching and compatibility code.

### 3. Presets are now clean constructor frontends

Preset constructors were migrated off legacy option/orchestrator paths and onto runtime-backed construction.

Examples:
- `NewMinimal`
- `NewSimpleInterop`
- `NewSingleChainInterop`
- two-L2 supernode presets
- flashblocks
- sync-tester
- conductor variants
- proof/superproof variants

The old “isolated” naming was dropped because it is no longer a special mode; it is now the default implementation model.

### 4. Orchestrator/system/control-plane architecture was removed

This PR deletes the legacy construction stack, including:
- `sysgo.Orchestrator`
- preset-side orchestrator wrappers
- control-plane bridge
- hydration path
- `ExtensibleSystem`
- `Registry`
- matcher-driven system lookup
- shim frontends
- `sysext`
- component ID plumbing
- remaining default-system ID bundles

The resulting framework is structurally constructor-first instead of “cleanroom layered on top of orchestrator.”

### 5. Preset/runtime APIs were simplified

Preset options are now cleanroom-native instead of `stack.Option[*sysgo.Orchestrator]`.

Runtime access also became more direct:
- runtime fields are public where presets need them
- preset assembly reads those fields directly
- a large number of runtime accessor/helper methods were removed

`devtest.P` was removed from the cleanroom option path in favor of `devtest.T`.

### 6. DSL and preset assembly moved to direct references

The DSL and preset layer no longer depend on registry/matcher lookup for normal construction:

- explicit primary refs are carried in DSL networks
- public RPC is explicit instead of looked up via matcher logic
- lifecycle is direct on the wrapped services/nodes
- mixed preset assembly uses explicit node/runtime data rather than synthetic CL/EL ID catalogs

### 7. Runtime layer was consolidated

The runtime layer was collapsed into a smaller set of shared families instead of 1:1 preset-shaped runtime roots.

Current runtime families:
- `SingleChainRuntime`
- `MultiChainRuntime`
- `MixedSingleChainRuntime`

Multi-chain internals were reorganized by the real axis of variation:
- supervisor-backed multichain runtime
- supernode-backed multichain runtime
- proofs as an overlay, not a separate topology root

Single-chain internals were reorganized around:
- a shared single-chain base runtime
- focused overlays for:
  - flashblocks
  - no-supervisor interop
  - follower/multinode variants
  - sync tester
  - conductors

## Notable Deletions

This PR removes a substantial amount of legacy framework code, including:
- `op-devstack/shim/*`
- `op-devstack/sysext/*`
- `op-devstack/stack/registry.go`
- `op-devstack/stack/component_id.go`
- `op-devstack/stack/orchestrator.go`
- `op-devstack/sysgo/orchestrator.go`
- `op-devstack/sysgo/system.go`
- legacy `system_*` constructor files
- external EL sync-tester paths
- many package-level `init_test.go` acceptance setup files

## Testing

Representative validation performed during this migration included:

```bash
go test ./op-devstack/presets ./op-devstack/sysgo -run '^$' -count=1
go test ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/... ./rust/kona/tests/... -run '^$' -count=1
go test ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/sync_tester/sync_tester_elsync -run TestSyncTesterELSync -count=1 -timeout 8m
go test ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/base/conductor -run TestConductorLeadershipTransfer -count=1 -timeout 8m
go test ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/flashblocks -run TestFlashblocksTransfer -count=1 -timeout 8m
go test ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/message -run TestInteropSystemSupervisor -count=1 -timeout 8m
go test ./rust/kona/tests/node/restart -run TestRestartSync -count=1 -timeout 8m
```

## Result

After this PR:

- acceptance tests instantiate their own target directly
- `op-devstack` no longer centers around orchestrator/system/registry abstractions
- constructor DAGs and direct references are the primary model
- legacy external/live-target and compatibility paths are removed
- the codebase is materially smaller and simpler

## Follow-up Work

This PR is intended as the architectural cutover. Follow-up cleanup can focus on smaller surface-level simplifications rather than major model changes. In particular:
- further tightening preset assembly where frontend construction still duplicates logic
- continued simplification of remaining `stack` interfaces that are now just thin compatibility shells

topPRs.title: feat(rust): karst-derive inlined derivation pipeline
topPRs.author: theochap
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Adds `kona-karst-derive`, a flat, inlined OP Stack derivation pipeline that replaces the staged `kona-derive` architecture
- Single `Pipeline` struct holds all intermediate state as fields; all derivation steps are direct method calls (no trait-based stage composition)
- Only supports **Holocene+**, removing all hardfork branching: always uses channel assembler, batch validator, Fjord size limits, and Holocene frame pruning
- Re-exports traits and error types from `kona-derive` for compatibility

### Key simplifications vs kona-derive

| kona-derive | karst-derive |
|---|---|
| `ChannelProvider` mux (bank vs assembler) | Always assembler (inline) |
| `BatchProvider` mux (queue vs validator) | Always validator (inline) |
| `BatchStream.is_active()` guard | Always active |
| `FrameQueue` conditional Holocene pruning | Always prune |
| Fjord vs Bedrock `MAX_RLP_BYTES_PER_CHANNEL` | Always Fjord (`100_000_000`) |
| Recursive signal-based reset | Single flat `reset()` method |

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check -p kona-karst-derive` compiles
- [x] `cargo clippy -p kona-karst-derive` passes with zero warnings
- [ ] Port key unit tests from kona-derive stages
- [ ] Integration testing with rollup node

topPRs.title: op-challenger: Replace supervisor with supernode in vm runner
topPRs.author: wwared
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Adds a new supernode RPC endpoint `superroot_syncStatus` which returns the aggregate values of all individual op-node's current `SyncStatus`es.

The new method is very similar to `superroot_atTimestamp` but this keeps them separate for now, though they could be combined in the future.

The response includes timestamps that could be used to call the `superroot_atTimestamp` method, but does not include the corresponding super root or optimistic L2 block data. I chose to make a simpler change for now, because I feel like these methods should be combined later, but if this is awkward let me know what other fields I should add (or remove) from the response.

I found #18947 as well, and the information mentioned in https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18947#issuecomment-3814030980 is there, but I'm not 100% sure about "sync status of every verification activity" - would appreciate if someone else can confirm/explain what that is.

**Tests**

Adds basic tests for the method and updates the vm runner test to use a `SuperNodeClient` instead.

**Metadata**

- Fixes #18669
- Fixes #18947
